concern_results.conclusion: host-smoke.sh now unsets CI, the peer CI flags, EXPECT_SOURCE_COMMIT and REQUIRE_CLEAN_RELEASE explicitly. The compgen loop now also catches GITHUB_* and CI_*. The script's own scoped CI=true and CI_COMMIT_SHA on the build line (122) run after the scrub, so the synthetic commit binding still works.
There is no new write path. The scrub only narrows the inherited environment, and HOME/XDG isolation is unchanged.

The stubs exit 9 when CI or release variables leak, and set -E plus the ERR trap reports the failing stage. The build stub allows only the scoped CI and CI_COMMIT_SHA, and only when CI_COMMIT_SHA matches the synthetic pattern.

This resolves the earlier P1 that the test only injected poison and never checked for it. The npm and agy stubs now assert that the leaked env is empty and log what they saw. The test checks the env audit log and the per-version release sourceCommit. If the GITHUB_* or CI unset were removed, the stub would exit 9 and the test would fail.
The change stays within A4's env-isolation scope, adds no flags, and keeps the stdout status tokens.
Only the test/smoke harness and docs change. Reverting is trivial and nothing irreversible happens.
The leak errors name the exact leaked variables. The JSONL logs give the test its evidence, and they are written only when the SMOKE_*_LOG variables are set.

Row 891 still says 16/16. The register is append-only, and the new row 892 explicitly replaces that count with 21/21 and <0.10s. plan.md now consistently says 21 mutants, and the AGENTS.md wording matches the script.
The release-binding boundary is contained. Outer GITHUB_SHA can no longer override the synthetic CI_COMMIT_SHA, and the test covers both the leak check and the commit binding.
The scripts/AGENTS.md rule was updated to match the script, and the change does not loosen it. The test uses isolated temp sandboxes, as test/AGENTS.md requires.
